coverage_claim: Covers the position as an occupant-independent work-slot: identity and keys, official and working titles, assigned duty content and essential functions, occupational classification and grade evaluation, unit/cost-centre placement and post-to-post reporting, work location plus geographic area or constituency, capacity and derived vacancy, funding and pay framing, requirements, delegated and prescribed authority, risk and screening, working conditions, lifecycle and effective-dated change, governance, evidence, and interoperability including declared profile choice and abstract-role binding. Evidence is the fourteen base sources plus grok-sourced Popolo, HL7 FHIR and schema.org Occupation/EmployeeRole references. No claim of universal completeness: occupancy, employment contract, payroll, recruiting workflow and the referenced taxonomies are owned elsewhere, and retention periods, unpaid/honorary posts, military billets, academic lines and most non-US civil-service regimes remain declared gaps.

boundary_decision.rationale: Both providers independently classify WM-ORG-004 as an entity and both anchor it on the same test: the record must be able to exist while vacant. That test is decidable, is grounded in W3C ORG (org:Post exists independently of the person filling it) and in the regulatory definition of a position as work assigned by competent authority, and it cleanly separates the seat from occupancy (WM-ORG-016), from the unit (WM-ORG-002), from the abstract role, and from the recruitment advertisement. No split or reclassification is warranted; the base boundary is adopted as written, with grok's word-sense and FHIR disambiguations carried forward as boundary annotations rather than as new structure.

add_findings.rationale: The base names org:Role only as an excluded neighbour and never records the edge from the seat to the abstract function any holder performs. Grok evidences this on W3C ORG (org:role on a Post), Popolo (many people fulfil the role CEO; one holds the post CEO at a named organization) and schema.org roleName as the occupancy-side analogue. It is non-duplicative of the base crosswalk finding, which maps internal job and grade structure to external classification schemes rather than binding a role, and it sits consistently in the alignment layer because the base itself declares role vocabularies to be alignments.

The base location finding covers duty station, work arrangement and jurisdiction derived from where the work is performed, but not the area a post is responsible for. Grok evidences a distinct construct on Popolo (post related to a constituency or territory, with abolition of the area eliminating the post) and schema.org occupationLocation (region for which the description is valid because requirements vary by jurisdiction). The base's own omissions list flags elected and appointed offices as only partially served, confirming the gap is material rather than stylistic.

The base records mapping strength and requires assessment evidence before claiming conformance, but never asks which vocabulary profile is in force for an instance. Grok evidences a real, source-backed contradiction between W3C ORG (org:holds/heldBy directly on a Post, Post as a subclass of Organization) and Popolo (org:holds forbidden, occupancy only through Membership), with FHIR PractitionerRole and schema.org Occupation as further profile choices. Declaring the profile per deployment is what converts that contradiction from a blocker into a governed configuration, so it belongs in the base alignment layer.

add_functions.rationale: The base function set covers establishment, classification, evaluation, capacity, requirements, authority, screening, occupancy reconciliation, amendment, certification, publication and freeze/abolish/dispose, but has no act that releases a vacant seat to recruitment. Narrowed to fill authorization only, so it does not overlap the base freeze-abolish-or-dispose function, this is the position-side handoff to the recruiting domain the base explicitly excludes, and it is the object a requisition or JobPosting references.

decisions.rationale: Claude offers a single decidable boundary test (everything true of a position while it is vacant), names the owning sibling model for each exclusion, carries roughly 1.4 times the base's own layer count in findings with four questions each, and declares one honest gap. Grok has more bundles and layers but nineteen findings across nineteen layers, so its topology is thinner per node despite the larger frame.

Independent agreement between providers plus the vacant-existence test grounded in W3C ORG and the regulatory definition of assigned work; nothing in either pack suggests an event, service or relationship framing would fit better.

decisions.disposition: rejected in favour of base topology
decisions.rationale: Grok's split of location, compensation and establishment into separate top-level bundles fragments concerns the base already integrates, and re-parenting the base's twenty-seven findings into nineteen thin layers would lose the base's explicit inline-only rationales without adding evidence.
Materially absent from the base, evidence-backed on ORG, Popolo and schema.org, and consistent with the base's own statement that role vocabularies are alignments rather than the position itself.

Distinct from duty station and work arrangement; Popolo ties post existence to area existence and schema.org scopes occupational description by region, and the base's omissions list already concedes elected and appointed offices are underserved.

The ORG-versus-Popolo disagreement about direct holds is genuine and source-backed; recording the profile in force per instance is the mechanism that keeps it a declared configuration rather than an unresolved contradiction.
Closes the only real hole in the base function set and marks the boundary handoff to the excluded recruiting domain; narrowed to fill so it does not duplicate the base freeze and abolish function.

decisions.concept: Grok class, series and grade finding
decisions.rationale: The base already separates occupational classification from grade and job evaluation across two findings with twelve questions and both a classification evaluation record and a job evaluation statement; grok adds no evidence the base lacks.

Covered by the base occupational-classification finding plus the version-pinned crosswalk finding, both of which already require scheme, version and mapping strength; the ISCO armed-forces-major-group nuance is deferred instead.

The base pay-range-and-transparency finding already fixes the position band against occupant pay and adds disclosure and reporting duties; only the unpaid, nominal-pay and fee-basis case is genuinely new and it is too thin to stand as structure, so it is deferred.

The base unit-and-cost-centre finding covers holding unit, legal entity, business unit and cost centre with movement semantics; the residual ex officio and Post-as-Organization dual-typing questions are deferred rather than injected.

decisions.disposition: rejected as split across existing layers
decisions.rationale: Its three elements land separately in the base screening-and-clearance, retention-and-privacy and pay findings; injecting it whole would create overlapping ownership of sensitivity and privacy rules across two bundles.

Both providers independently refuse to persist occupancy on the seat and both cite ORG and the assignment boundary; the base's no-artifact rationale is kept because a stored vacancy flag would create a second source of truth against WM-ORG-016.

Grok marks retention covered while its own notes concede national schedules were not fetched; the base's gap marking is the accurate one and no fetched primary source in either pack states a retention period for position records.

decisions.disposition: re-key all source ids on merge
decisions.rationale: SRC-002 denotes HR Open in the base and Popolo in grok, and several other identifiers collide across providers while pointing at different documents; the synthesizer must re-key rather than union by identifier or every accepted addition will carry the wrong citation.

decisions.disposition: carried as boundary annotation, not structure
decisions.rationale: Grok's align-not-equate treatment of PractitionerRole and its exclusion of financial, geospatial and sports senses of position are correct and useful, but they are boundary prose rather than findings; they are recorded as a publication hold on the boundary notes instead of being injected as nodes.

publication_holds: Source verification is incomplete: every base URL and version pin must be re-resolved at publication time. In particular the base cites 5 CFR and 29 CFR from the Cornell LII reproduction because eCFR and opm.gov were unreachable in its run, while grok reached eCFR current as of 2026-08-20 and the OPM classification standards PDF; re-verify and dual-cite or swap to the official host before publishing.

Source identifiers collide across providers with different underlying documents (SRC-002 is HR Open in the base and Popolo in grok, among others). All sources must be re-keyed during merge and every accepted addition re-pointed, and the merged source list re-verified as live, before any draft is published.

ISO 30400:2022 must not be cited as defining position, job, role or FTE: grok's own note concedes the term text was not inspectable behind the paywall, so only the standard's existence, date and scope are supportable. The ISCO-08 citation must likewise resolve to an authoritative ILO or UNSD host rather than the third-party netlify mirror used by grok.

Retention and disposition periods remain a declared gap. No fetched primary source in either pack states a retention period for position records, descriptions or classification decisions; the structure may be published only as a required local determination, never as canonical guidance.

Multi-profile domain validation is outstanding. Evidence concentrates on US federal General Schedule classification, UK FCA prescribed responsibilities, EU pay transparency and a single HCM vendor API. Before publication the model must be exercised against at least a civic or legislative profile (Popolo post with constituency), a healthcare profile (FHIR PractitionerRole unnamed slot) and a non-US private-sector profile, and every regional assumption must be labelled a jurisdiction profile rather than a universal requirement.

Published boundary notes must carry grok's disambiguations verbatim in substance: HL7 FHIR PractitionerRole is aligned, not equated, to a classified position, and the financial, geospatial and sports senses of the word position are excluded, including schema.org's Quarterback example of a named position.
deferred_research: Post-as-Organization dual typing and ex officio membership conferred by holding a post (W3C ORG and Popolo), unresolved against the WM-ORG-002 unit and WM-ORG-003 team boundaries and against corporate statutory officer roles versus board membership.

Unpaid, honorary, nominal-pay, fee-basis, piece-work and volunteer positions, and statutory exclusions from classification and pay statutes such as 5 U.S.C. section 5102(c); currently only reachable through grok's rejected remuneration finding.

Military billets versus rank as personal status (including ISCO Major Group 0 alignment), academic faculty lines and endowed chairs, and elected or appointed public office appointment and eligibility rules.
Works council, co-determination and collective consultation duties triggered by position creation, reclassification and abolition; no primary source was verified by either provider.
Occupancy of a position by a non-human agent, unresolved in both packs even though org:holds is defined over agents rather than persons.
National retention schedules (for example NARA GRS) and GDPR storage-limitation periods as concrete durations for position descriptions, classification files and occupant-linked records.

Unfetched standard texts that would strengthen weakly supported areas: HR Open Position and PositionOpening full schemas, the ESCO occupation pillar beyond its ISCO mapping, ISO 30414 human capital metrics, and ISO 30400 term entries.
Dual-incumbency overlap windows for succession, career-ladder or intern positions, job-share fractions and union exclusivity of a slot, all widely practised but without primary support in either run.
